families.family: many final (non‑prerelease) versions after the first final
families.why: The new helper streams final versions directly once a final is seen, while the old code buffered every final version into a list before returning an iterator.
families.size_meaning: n = number of final versions yielded
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # n final versions, all non‑prerelease
    versions = [f"1.{i}" for i in range(n)]
    # filter is called as spec_set.filter(iterable, prereleases=None, key=None)
    return [(versions, None, None)]

families.why: The refactored _pep440_filter_prereleases streams final releases as soon as the first final is seen, avoiding buffering the entire tail of the iterable. For a large stream of non‑prerelease versions that appears after an early final release, the new code can start yielding immediately, reducing peak memory and latency.
families.size_meaning: number of version strings after the first final release

families.why: Many pre‑release versions appear before the first final release. The new lazy filter buffers only until the first final version, then streams the rest, while the old filter buffers the whole input before deciding which list to return.

def make(n):
    # n pre‑release versions, then one final, then two more finals
    items = [f"1.0.{i}a1" for i in range(n)] + ["2.0.0", "2.0.1", "2.0.2"]
    # SpecifierSet.filter is called positionally: (iterable, prereleases=None, key=None)
    return [[items, None, None]]

families.family: many arbitrary (non‑version) strings before any final version
families.why: The new _pep440_filter_prereleases appends each arbitrary string to *two* lists (arbitrary_strings and all_nonfinal) before the first final, then later iterates over arbitrary_strings when the first final appears. The old code appended each arbitrary string to a single list only.
families.size_meaning: n = number of arbitrary strings before the first final version
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # n arbitrary strings that only match an '===' specifier, then a final version
    arbitrary = [f"arb{i}" for i in range(n)]
    final = ["1.0"]
    iterable = arbitrary + final
    return [(iterable, None, None)]

families.why: After the first final release the new implementation yields each subsequent final release via a Python generator (`yield item`). The old implementation buffered all final releases in a list and returned `iter(list)`, which is iterated in C and is faster per element. For a very long tail of final releases this per‑yield overhead can make the new version slower.
families.size_meaning: number of version strings after the first final release
